title: Fit an elastic-edged cover on a tabletop ironing board
instruction: Fit the padded cover over the ironing board. Tuck the elastic edge under both ends and leave the ironing surface flat.
context: The gathered seam at the nose holds a replacement cover as you stretch the other end over the steel rim. Counterhold the cover while each elastic end retracts under the deck so the finished ironing surface stays flat and centred.
setup: A 73 × 32 cm tabletop ironing board stands on four rubber feet with its steel deck 10.5 cm above the worktop. The left YAM arm faces the tapered nose and the right faces the broad heel. A matching cotton cover with a 6 mm foam pad lies face up on the deck. Both gathered elastic seams start loose, 57 mm inboard from the ends. The rims are bare beneath the board. Start both YAM grippers open and clear. The README lists tabletop positions.
scoring: Score 1.0 if both elastic seam midpoints stay 1–15 mm below the deck underside and 13–79 mm inboard of their ends, within 15 mm of the board centreline. Require the pad centre within 12 mm of deck centre along both axes, four surface checks within 12 mm of installed height, and both hands clear for 1 s. Score 0.5 for a released cover with at least one hem tucked to the same geometry before all full-credit conditions are met, and 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: Rest both ends of the cover on the deck, with each elastic seam above the surface, 57 mm inboard from the nearest end. Leave the board bare beneath both rims. Flatten the center pad without stretching the elastic.
fidelity: The full-size steel deck supports a replaceable padded cover. Native spring-loaded sliders model the elastic seams, which collide with the fingers and catch under the deck. The pad makes native contacts with the grippers and deck. The rendered fabric skin follows the actual pad and seam poses. The model omits local wrinkles and distributed stretch.
scores: Demo: 1.0 after 553 actions. Dream-1: 0 after 600 actions.
